x: This race promised to be a 'cracker' with Adrian Cook facing stiff opposition from new members Michael Manning and John Flynn. Unfortunately John came off his motor bike the day before and although he was not hurt, he was shaken and bruised, and understandably left the fight for first place to the other two.
Michael Manning (64), who has become one of our leading Youths this winter, and David Bailey (50), another promising youngster, warm up for the Boxing Day 2 miles handicap.
Michael Manning's run was a good effort and new member M.Bentley did extremely well running through the mud in a pair of flat shoes in his first run in our colours and making the scoring four.
Michael Manning · Running · David Hayter · Running

Junior, Simon Holmes, got up into the respectable half of the field and Michael Manning, a youth, brought comfort to those of us looking for some new Belgrave talent with a splendid first time run in this event.

Our apologies to Michael Manning. In our last issue we reported that he had won the Youths cross country championship, which of course he did, but unfortunately the report was headed 'Adrian Cook wins Youths Championship'.

He has only run this event three times but has improved from 10m.44secs. to 10m.5.8secs., and finally, Michael Manning, who although still a Junior has turned out in a couple of 5,000 metres league races and has run very well.
Two youngsters also making promising first appearances were David Didino who reached 3rd in the 'B' high jump, and Michael Manning who gained a similar position in the 5,000 metres.

… under 2 minutes, Colin Pearson - a good double performance, another best from Leo Coy, youngsters Ronnie McCrossen and Michael Manning, two very good relay runs, Paul Whitby's hurdles, Paul Williamson's two excellent runs, and of course Snowy's eight events.…

In appalling conditions Simon Holmes just scraped home ahead of Michael Manning to win the 'Savage Shield' by one second! Behind these two the battle for the third place medal was just as fierce.

Michael Manning's 2,000 metres steeplechase proved the highlight. He did his normal trick of loping along at the rear of the field to start with and then working through until at the tape only eight tenths of a second separated him from the winner.
P.Gardner 2:17.1; M.Manning 2:17.5. YOUTHS. 400m: nq D.Bailey 56.6. 200m: nq D.Bailey 25.9.

Another youngster who seems to have been with us for ages and who continues to progress relentlessly is Adrian Cook, who took the 800m and then followed it up for good measure with 2nd, behind Michael Manning, in the 1,500m and 2nd in the high jump.
Competing in a composite team: W.Laws 16:04; M.Manning 15:22. Fastest laps: R.Holt (HER) 13:28; R.Gevers (SLH) 13:59; W.Upcott (SLH) 14:04 ... 5th fastest J.Stow (BEL) 14:06.

Both turned in times considerably faster than their spring performances in the championship race. Michael Manning continued his progress towards the top and two other youngsters to run well were Simon Williamson and Pete Gardner.

In the Junior race Pete Gardner managed for the first time to get narrowly ahead of Simon Williamson, and Michael Manning also ran well up in 14th position.

Mick Manning, last year's winner of the longer race found it a tough afternoon placing 2nd in the 1,500m after being shunted to 3rd in the two lap event by Peter North who startingly revealed some real fight.

Lionel Mann and Mick Manning have also put up their best times this year in the steeplechase and with Alan Black regularly in action Leo Coy had to wait for an odd 400 metres to make his 1976 league debut!
Michael Manning turned up to comfortably cover the two laps of the Junior race for the "Savage Shield". What a pity we had not seen him in action for us earlier in the season.
